name: Perez-Marrero DMSO
question: Does intravesical dimethyl sulfoxide improve symptoms and objective measures more than saline in patients with interstitial cystitis?

design.blinding: Objective-response assessors blinded; recognizable DMSO garlic odor limited patient blinding
design.population: Thirty women and three men with biopsies suggestive of interstitial cystitis were enrolled; mean age was 48 years and mean symptom duration was 5.5 years. None had Hunner ulcers or contracted bladders.
design.locator: Full text, Materials and Methods, pp 36-37; Discussion, p 39

verdictNote: First-period subjective and objective responses favored DMSO; exact P values were not reported.
takeaway: In a randomized crossover trial of intravesical 50% dimethyl sulfoxide versus saline for interstitial cystitis, first-period marked subjective improvement was 6/15 (40%) versus 3/17 (18%), and objective improvement was 14/15 (93%) versus 6/17 (35%).

reports.label: Controlled crossover comparison
reports.dateLocator: PubMed citation, July 1988; day not reported
reports.citation: Perez-Marrero R, Emerson LE, Feltis JT. "A Controlled Study of Dimethyl Sulfoxide in Interstitial Cystitis." *J Urol.* 1988;140(1):36-39. doi:10.1016/s0022-5347(17)41478-9
reports.followUp: After four instillations at 2-week intervals in each period, separated by a 4-week rest
reports.followUpLocator: Full text, Materials and Methods, pp 36-37

results.measure: First-period patient-rated marked improvement after four instillations; analyzed patients
results.note: No primary endpoint or numerical effect estimate, confidence interval, P value, or significance threshold was specified; the authors state that the subjective differences were statistically significant. The 53% figure is 8/15 after DMSO-to-saline crossover.
results.locator: Full text, Table 5 and Results, p 38

results.measure: First-period improvement adjudicated by blinded assessors using urodynamics, voiding charts, and symptom scales; analyzed patients
results.note: Objective response required a 50% increase in cystometric urge or capacity and/or loss of filling pain, supported by improvement in the voiding chart or symptom scales. No numerical effect estimate, confidence interval, P value, or significance threshold was specified.
results.locator: Full text, Materials and Methods, p 37; Table 4, p 38

results.measure: First-period patient-rated moderate or marked improvement; analyzed patients
results.note: Sum of the moderate and marked categories; no separate P value or confidence interval reported.

results.measure: Second-period patient-rated marked improvement by original randomized sequence; 15 patients per sequence evaluated
results.note: Second-period values reflect treatment sequences, not a concurrent DMSO-versus-saline comparison.
results.locator: Full text, Table 5 and Results, p 38

results.measure: Second-period objective improvement by original randomized sequence; 15 patients per sequence evaluated
results.note: The text prints 86% for 13/15, while 13/15 rounds to 87%; one initial DMSO responder relapsed. Second-period values reflect treatment sequences, not a concurrent DMSO-versus-saline comparison.
results.locator: Full text, Table 4 and Results, p 38

harms.label: Complications during the instillation study
harms.note: 5/33 patients (15%) had complications. Three minor events did not interrupt therapy: 2/33 had uncomplicated lower urinary tract infections and 1/33 had biliary colic. Clavien-Dindo grades, retention, reoperation, and mesh exposure were not reported.

harms.label: Severe neurologic symptoms requiring treatment discontinuation
harms.note: 2/33 randomized patients, both during saline: one hemiparesis and one severe migraine. Both resolved within 48 hours; the authors reported no significant side effects attributable to DMSO.

delivery.label: Instillation schedule
delivery.value: 50 cc of 50% dimethyl sulfoxide or normal saline intravesically every 2 weeks for four instillations, then a 4-week rest and crossover to four instillations of the other solution; hold in the bladder for at least 15 minutes. An outpatient nurse administered all instillations.
delivery.locator: Full text, Materials and Methods, pp 36-37
delivery.note: Thirty-three randomized; 15 DMSO-first and 18 saline-first. One saline-first patient was removed after pregnancy following the first instillation; 32 were analyzed in period 1, and 15 per sequence entered period 2.
